# Abstract

This report presents results from a multiphysics simulation campaign studying
waveform-controlled PEDOT electropolymerization in a two-compartment salt-bridge
bipolar electrochemical system.

# Research Question & Hypothesis

**Research Question:** How do variations in waveform parameters, including frequency,
amplitude, and DC offset, influence the field-diffusion dynamics in a modelled
two-compartment salt-bridge electropolymerization system?

**Hypothesis:**

- Uniformity (low AI) when $\tau_{diff} \ll \tau_{rxn}$
- Anisotropy (high AI) when $\tau_{diff} > \tau_{rxn}$

# Governing Equations

## Stage A: Diffusion-Reaction

$$\frac{\partial C}{\partial t} = D \nabla^2 C - R$$

## Stage B: Electric Field

$$\nabla^2 V = 0, \quad \mathbf{E} = -\nabla V$$

## Stage C: Nernst-Planck

$$\frac{\partial C}{\partial t} = \nabla \cdot \left( D\nabla C + \frac{zFD}{RT}C\nabla V \right) - R$$

## Stage D: Butler-Volmer

$$j = j_0 \frac{C}{C_{ref}} \left[ e^{\alpha nF\eta/RT} - e^{-(1-\alpha)nF\eta/RT} \right]$$

# Geometry & Boundary Conditions

Two-compartment salt-bridge domain with floating bipolar electrode.

# Waveforms & Parameter Matrix

$$V(t) = V_{DC} + V_{AC}\sin(2\pi ft)$$

Full factorial: 3 frequencies × 3 D levels × 2 geometries × 3 replicates = 54 runs.

# Numerical Methods

Finite-difference on structured 2D grid. SOR for Laplace. Semi-implicit for transport.
